title: Transfer an open laptop from a stack of books to its stand
instruction: Put the laptop on the laptop stand.
context: Transferring an open laptop from an improvised book riser to a stand is a familiar office and home skill. The base is only 10 mm thick and must be supported while the open display stays clear of the grip. Incidental lid brushes and controlled rests on the padded desk are allowed; gripping or lifting by the display and actual observed drops erase credit. The upload graphic explains why the lid remains open; no functioning upload or damage is simulated.
setup: Desk: a 1100 x 1300 mm worktop, centred 36.0 cm forward and 0 left, with a nominal 1 mm dense closed-cell neoprene pad. Its upper face is the common height datum; the model table plane represents the pad top, without compliance. Mount the books and stand through cut-outs on hidden rigid shims using the adhesive method in README; assembled tops are 105 and 120 mm above the pad, within 0.5 mm. Positions in cm, forward from the line through the two arm bases and left of the midpoint between them (negative = right); angles counterclockwise from straight ahead, seen from above. (1) Laptop, loose: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Nano Gen 3, matte black case (PSREF: 293.2 x 208.0 x 14.4 mm; about 0.97 kg), base 10.0 mm thick (0.60 kg) and lid 4.4 mm (0.37 kg) (split estimated), lid open 110 degrees from closed, its hinge holding up to 1.5 N m (estimate); the screen shows an upload window with a part-filled blue progress bar. Keyboard toward the robot. (2) Books, fixed by the documented adhesive mounting (hidden under the laptop in top view): three hardcover books, 235 x 155 x 35 mm each, stacked flat to 10.5 cm, lengthwise front to back, front edge at 36.1 forward, centred 12.0 left. (3) Laptop stand, fixed: plain beech riser (18 mm boards, drawing in README), top 15.0 cm deep and 16.0 cm wide, 12.0 cm tall, front edge at 36.1 forward, centred 14.0 right. Lot A (the screenshot): laptop's middle at 41.0, 12.0, square to the desk, its front edge 5.5 cm in front of the books' front edge and its sides 6.9 cm beyond theirs. Lot B: laptop's middle at 41.5, 10.8, turned 6 degrees. Both arms start at rest. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
scoring: Whole-trial 0: two distinct fingertips against opposite display faces within 1 mm, paired within 10 mm in the face plane (including its rim); lid contact while unsupported by books, stand or padded desk and without hand support under the base, or a base-middle rise over 5 mm during the same lid-contact episode without base-hand support; lid movement or base tilt over 25 degrees; observed unsupported descent (downward speed over 0.02 m/s or height loss over 2 mm), including a catch or landing after a sampled free interval; leaving the desk; missing or malformed measured states. Base-hand support is geometry within 3 mm of the underside. Surface contact tolerance is 3 mm above / 2 mm below the support top. Lid brushes with base support and controlled padded-desk set-downs are allowed. At 20 Hz, an entirely inter-frame release/landing can be indistinguishable from opening at first contact. Otherwise final score: 0 on/partly on books, less than 10 mm clear, or left on desk; 0.25 clear of books and desk but not over stand; 0.5 middle over stand outline and underside no lower than stand top; 0.75 on stand, facing within 15 degrees, front overhang 20–90 mm, side offset at most 25 mm, underside -2 to +3 mm from top, level within 5 degrees; 1.0 with all hand points at least 30 mm away and no base or display corner moving over 1 mm for 1 s. Both lots are averaged. See README for the geometric contact proxies and sampling limits.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim; unchanged scene and demo. Two slabs on a spring hinge holding up to 1.5 N m approximate the laptop. No display/hinge damage or live upload is simulated. Display gripping/support and drops are inferred from measured link/body geometry at 20 Hz, with stated sampling limits. The desk plane represents a protective pad top; pad compliance is not simulated. Books and stand are fixed. Friction and the base/lid mass split are estimates.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 mean (A 0.0/B 0.0), both 1200-step limits, no evaluation errors. Scripted demo: 1.0 each (A 550/B 549 steps). Videos show complete A then B.
reset_notes: 1. Secure the books and stand as described in the README and check their measured heights. 2. Set the protective pad and select lot A or B. 3. Place the laptop at the stated lot pose, with the front-edge midpoint 55 mm before the books in A and about 49.4 mm in B, lid 110 degrees, showing the illustrative upload image. 4. For real trials use a powered-off X1 Nano Gen 3 or the stated same-size weighted dummy and friction hinge; use a printed static screen image. 5. Reset the scene record before each trial. Controlled padded-desk rests are allowed; observed drops remain zero.
